The summary or encounter note retains its clinical source while becoming available alongside regional information; consolidation does not transfer the GP's professional authority to the platform.

elements.name: Primary Care Notification Dispatch

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-02`: **Primary Care Notification Dispatch**: Dispatch emergency department arrival, acute admission, and discharge notifications to the patient's registered general practitioner.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Dispatch emergency department arrival, acute admission, and discharge notifications to the patient's registered general practitioner.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Primary-care notifications inform the registered GP of significant acute-care events. This outward notification responsibility is distinct from querying a chronic-care timeline: the latter shares context but has no established equivalence to dispatching the required arrival, admission or discharge notice.

elements.name: Acute Clinical State Event Capture

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-03`: **Acute Clinical State Event Capture**: Ingest clinical deterioration notifications and acute clinical status updates.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Ingest clinical deterioration notifications and acute clinical status updates.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Acute-state capture records deterioration notifications and current clinical status as externally established information. Approved reusable clinical-information composition is sufficient for this responsibility; routing a critical-result alert does not become a specialised capture Function merely because both concern urgent care.

elements.name: Acute Care Clinical Context Provision

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-04`: **Acute Care Clinical Context Provision**: Provide consolidated longitudinal history and active medication lists to acute care clinicians at point of triage.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Provide consolidated longitudinal history and active medication lists to acute care clinicians at point of triage.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Acute context provision brings relevant history and active medications together for clinicians facing a current presentation. It supports rapid understanding without substituting the consolidated view for clinical assessment, triage or a decision about treatment.

elements.name: Emergency Department Arrival & Triage Ingestion

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-05`: **Emergency Department Arrival & Triage Ingestion**: Ingest emergency presentation, triage category, and chief complaint records.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Ingest emergency presentation, triage category, and chief complaint records.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Emergency presentation ingestion retains the arrival, triage category and presenting complaint reported by the emergency context. It makes that event available for regional correlation while preserving that the clinical triage judgement was established by the responsible source.

elements.name: Emergency Care Cross-Facility Correlation

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-06`: **Emergency Care Cross-Facility Correlation**: Correlate incoming emergency presentations with recent regional admissions, prior discharge summaries, and known allergy profiles.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Correlate incoming emergency presentations with recent regional admissions, prior discharge summaries, and known allergy profiles.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Cross-facility correlation connects an emergency presentation with relevant recent history and allergy information. It supports situational understanding across institutional boundaries without deciding the clinical significance of the combined evidence or assigning emergency treatment.

elements.name: Inpatient Rounding Context Provision

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-07`: **Inpatient Rounding Context Provision**: Aggregate diagnostic results, current medication administration records, and nursing notes for multidisciplinary inpatient rounds.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Aggregate diagnostic results, current medication administration records, and nursing notes for multidisciplinary inpatient rounds.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Rounding context brings results, medication records and nursing notes into an accessible multidisciplinary view. Assembly serves the clinical discussion but does not perform rounds, determine pending clinical work or establish the team's professional conclusions.

elements.name: Inpatient Clinical Progression Tracking

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-08`: **Inpatient Clinical Progression Tracking**: Capture inpatient clinical milestone completions (e.g., medical stability achieved, allied health clearance).

elements.governed_definition_latex: Capture inpatient clinical milestone completions (e.g., medical stability achieved, allied health clearance).

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Inpatient progression tracking captures clinical milestones reported by the responsible participants. General clinical-information capabilities and configured workflow composition suffice for the established Feature; capture does not require inventing a specialised Function or make Harmonia the authority declaring clinical stability.

elements.name: Laboratory & Imaging Result Distribution

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-09`: **Laboratory & Imaging Result Distribution**: Reliably distribute structured diagnostic reports (pathology, radiology) to ordering clinicians and designated secondary recipients.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Reliably distribute structured diagnostic reports (pathology, radiology) to ordering clinicians and designated secondary recipients.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Result distribution connects established diagnostic reports with ordering and designated secondary recipients. It supports continuity of diagnostic information across care settings while retaining the distinction between delivery, recipient review and the clinical decision based on the result.

elements.name: Diagnostic History Consolidation

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-10`: **Diagnostic History Consolidation**: Consolidate historical diagnostic trends (e.g., cumulative laboratory results) across multiple regional providers into an integrated view.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Consolidate historical diagnostic trends (e.g., cumulative laboratory results) across multiple regional providers into an integrated view.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Diagnostic history consolidation makes prior evidence visible across regional providers. A combined historical view can support comparison over time without itself establishing a diagnostic interpretation, reconciling conflicting clinical assertions or replacing each report's source standing.

elements.name: Medication History Reconciliation Ingestion

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-11`: **Medication History Reconciliation Ingestion**: Ingest reconciled medication histories compiled during clinical transitions of care.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Ingest reconciled medication histories compiled during clinical transitions of care.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: This Feature receives medication histories already reconciled by clinical participants during care transitions. The platform preserves and connects that account; ingestion is distinct from performing the clinical reconciliation or independently deciding which regimen is correct.

elements.name: Medication Administration Tracking

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-12`: **Medication Administration Tracking**: Distribute medication therapy orders, dispensing updates, and administration records across clinical care boundaries.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Distribute medication therapy orders, dispensing updates, and administration records across clinical care boundaries.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Medication tracking conveys orders, dispensing changes and administration information across care boundaries while keeping their meanings separate. This supports a coherent therapy account without treating a supplied medicine as an administered dose or a distributed order as treatment performed.

elements.name: Immunisation Event Submission

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-13`: **Immunisation Event Submission**: Ingest point-of-care immunisation administration records and syndicate to national immunization registers.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Ingest point-of-care immunisation administration records and syndicate to national immunization registers.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Immunisation submission connects a source-recorded administration event with the national register context. It supports continuity and reporting without performing the immunisation or making successful transmission equivalent to every downstream registry outcome.

elements.name: Screening Recall Notification Distribution

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-14`: **Screening Recall Notification Distribution**: Distribute clinical screening reminders and recall notices to designated healthcare providers.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Distribute clinical screening reminders and recall notices to designated healthcare providers.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Screening recall distribution conveys established reminders to the designated care providers. Its notification responsibility is expressible through approved event and workflow composition; the catalogue does not invent a specialised Function or transfer the clinical decision to recall the patient.

elements.name: Community Encounter Ingestion

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-15`: **Community Encounter Ingestion**: Ingest home visit notes, community nursing observations, and social support assessments.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Ingest home visit notes, community nursing observations, and social support assessments.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Community encounter ingestion brings home-visit and community assessments into the longitudinal information context. It supports continuity across organisational boundaries while preserving source attribution and the difference between the documentation received and care performed by the platform.

elements.name: Community Care Plan Synchronization

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-16`: **Community Care Plan Synchronization**: Synchronize community care plan updates between hospital outreach teams and community health organizations.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Synchronize community care plan updates between hospital outreach teams and community health organizations.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Community plan synchronisation keeps hospital outreach and community participants informed of established plan changes. It supports shared clinical intent without allowing synchronisation to become authority to choose that intent or allocate clinical work.

elements.name: Outreach Visit Context Provision

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-17`: **Outreach Visit Context Provision**: Package and deliver portable clinical summaries and offline-capable care summaries for remote outreach clinics.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Package and deliver portable clinical summaries and offline-capable care summaries for remote outreach clinics.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Outreach context provision prepares portable summaries for care beyond the usual connected environment. Their usefulness depends on retaining clinical and temporal context; an offline-capable copy is not automatically current authoritative state or a new origin of clinical facts.

elements.name: Outreach Encounter Outcome Ingestion

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-18`: **Outreach Encounter Outcome Ingestion**: Ingest and reconcile clinical documentation gathered during rural and remote outreach visits.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Ingest and reconcile clinical documentation gathered during rural and remote outreach visits.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Outreach outcome ingestion brings documentation collected during remote visits back into the governed record. It reconnects previously separated activity with the regional context without erasing when, where and by whom the source information was established.

elements.name: Remote Telemetry Ingestion

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-19`: **Remote Telemetry Ingestion**: Ingest home patient monitoring data, biometric telemetry, and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs).

elements.governed_definition_latex: Ingest home patient monitoring data, biometric telemetry, and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs).

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Remote telemetry ingestion accepts measurements and patient-reported contributions from outside the usual care site. The information can inform subsequent monitoring and interpretation, but acquisition alone does not establish clinical significance or authorise an intervention.

elements.name: Virtual Care Session Context Binding

sources.text: - `FEAT-SD-20`: **Virtual Care Session Context Binding**: Associate synchronous virtual/telehealth consultations with the longitudinal health record and active care episode.

elements.governed_definition_latex: Associate synchronous virtual/\allowbreak{}telehealth consultations with the longitudinal health record and active care episode.

baseline_description.Feature Overview: Virtual-session binding associates a consultation with the enduring record and the relevant episode. It preserves the clinical context across delivery modes without turning the communication session itself into proof of clinical conclusions or adequacy of care.

sources.text: - `FEAT-HSO-16`: **Mobile Worker Task Dispatch**: Dispatch community care tasks and urgent visits to roving clinicians' mobile devices.

elements.name: Governed Assurance

sources.text: ### Governed Assurance

elements.governed_definition_latex: The capability to independently evaluate a governed subject against applicable assurance criteria through the assembly and evaluation of sufficient trustworthy evidence, establishing explicit findings, exceptions and assurance conclusions.

baseline_description.Capability Overview:
Governed Assurance independently evaluates a subject through applicable criteria and trustworthy evidence, establishing explicit findings and conclusions. Context establishment associates source-owned information with a particular assurance purpose; assessment evaluates it; adjudication establishes the supported outcome. Insufficient evidence remains a meaningful limit rather than a forced positive or negative result.

The capability can manage its own assurance activity without managing the subject. Request, progression status and established outcome are different client concerns; the requester does not thereby control the evaluation or gain unrestricted status access.
baseline_description.Boundary: No remediation, assignment or operational escalation of the subject is acquired. Financial governance is deliberately excluded; assurance does not recursively assure its own execution, and no component allocation is established.
baseline_description.Harmonia Architectural Relevance: Formal classification remains Unresolved. The approved independent-assurance responsibility and contribution model establish material purpose without resolving that metadata dimension.

elements.placement_rationale: The responsibility concerns associate trustworthy evidence, assess it and adjudicate independently reportable findings about governed service behaviour. It is the finest capability frame required for the established behaviour; the older contextual heading is not another capability tier.

elements.name: Design Service Assurance

sources.text: #### Design Service Assurance

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Design Service Assurance}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Defines how satisfaction of a governed requirement, constraint or expected behaviour is to be independently established, including the applicable assurance disposition, assurance criteria, required evidence and evaluation expectations.



\item 
\textbf{Boundary}: Concerns assurance design. It does not establish the underlying governance requirement, grant authority to it, perform the resulting assurance, manage the subject activity or prescribe application or implementation mechanisms. Modelling the resulting Assurance Definition does not grant approval authority. The Strategy peer relationship to behaviour design and failure/\allowbreak{}recovery design creates no additional Capability or Function.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Function Overview: Designing service assurance turns a requirement's assurance question into an explicit disposition and evaluation basis. The modeller determines how satisfaction is to be assessed, not what the authoritative requirement should mean or who may approve it. Design completion is not evidence that the implemented behaviour satisfies that requirement.

elements.name: Manage Assurance Criteria

sources.text: #### Manage Assurance Criteria

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Manage Assurance Criteria}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Establishes and manages reusable, governed and temporally identifiable assurance criteria through which governed subjects may be evaluated.



\item 
\textbf{Scope}: Criteria may express governance rule boundaries, quality constraints, performance expectations, compliance criteria, temporal criteria, evidence requirements or completeness expectations. These examples are not an exhaustive taxonomy. Criteria may have lifecycle, version and temporal applicability.



\item 
\textbf{Boundary}: Managing a criterion does not transfer authority for the governing requirement from which it may derive. Criteria may operationalise a requirement without silently altering, weakening, strengthening or replacing it; not every criterion must derive from formal Governance. Modelling/\allowbreak{}managing criteria does not inherently confer approval authority. Detailed criterion lifecycle states and approval workflows remain unresolved.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Function Overview: Criteria management maintains the reusable evaluative basis and its temporal standing. It permits an assessment to be understood against the criterion applicable at the relevant time, rather than today's unqualified version. Management of that basis does not inherently grant approval authority or permit alteration of the governing obligation.

elements.name: Establish Assurance Context

sources.text: #### Establish Assurance Context

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Establish Assurance Context}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Establishes the governed subject, applicable assurance purpose and criteria, relevant temporal context, and contextual association of sufficient trustworthy source information as evidence required for an assurance activity.



\item 
\textbf{Scope}: Includes the evidence-assembly responsibility previously described as Assurance Evidence Assembly; no separate evidence-assembly Function is established. Sufficiency is required for conclusion, not assumed merely because context is established; unavailable or insufficient evidence remains explicit.



\item 
\textbf{Information Boundary}: Source information remains owned by its responsible source Capability. Its use as evidence does not transfer ownership or originating authority. Governed Assurance owns the contextual association that particular information constitutes evidence for a particular assurance purpose. Evidence association and applicable criteria may each be temporal and version-specific; association distinguishes the information state relevant to assurance from its current state.



\item 
\textbf{Realisation Boundary}: Uses generic EC-02 context-management capability together with EC-14 assurance-specific semantics as documented in \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#41-context-management-contribution}{§4.1}. Establishment of Assurance Context prescribes no copying, persistence, aggregation, caching or other technical mechanism.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Function Overview: Context establishment makes particular source-owned information evidence for a particular assurance purpose, with applicable subject, criteria and time identified. It includes evidence assembly without assuming sufficiency or prescribing copying and storage. This contextual evidentiary association is the assurance responsibility; ownership of the source material remains unchanged.

elements.adjudication_note: HUMAN ADJUDICATION REQUIRED: Canonical assurance against a governed subject is not independent review of the assurance service itself.

elements.name: Adjudicate Assurance Assessment

sources.text: #### Adjudicate Assurance Assessment

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Adjudicate Assurance Assessment}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Determines the assurance finding or conclusion that follows from the assessed evidence and applicable assurance criteria.



\item 
\textbf{Boundary}: Establishment of the finding/\allowbreak{}conclusion is part of adjudication. It remains distinct from evidence assessment, operational response, remediation, escalation, workflow progression and clinical judgement. No separate conclusion-establishment or reporting Function is introduced merely because a conclusion is established or may be communicated.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Function Overview: Adjudication establishes the supported finding or conclusion from assessed detail. It is distinct from gathering evidence and from reporting an outcome already reached. Insufficiency must remain explicit rather than be forced into satisfaction or non-satisfaction, and the resulting finding does not acquire authority to remediate the subject.

elements.name: Request Service Assurance

sources.text: ### 5.1 Request Service Assurance

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Request Service Assurance}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Enables an authorised consumer to request that Service Assurance be performed for an applicable governed subject in accordance with an established Assurance Definition.



\item 
\textbf{Approved Consumers}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Care Coordinator}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{Service Coordinator}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{Regulator}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{Policy Authority}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{System Steward}}.



\item 
\textbf{Associated Interaction}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md\#service-assurance-request}{Service Assurance Request}, with Service Guardian and one authorised requesting Role.



\item 
\textbf{Process Relationship}: Requests \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md\#assurance-process-execution}{Assurance Process Execution} under an applicable established Assurance Definition. It does not require a new Assurance Process Design instance for each request.



\item 
\textbf{Independence Boundary}: The requesting Role identifies the assurance need within its responsibility and authority. Requesting does not grant authority to define or alter the Assurance Definition, alter Assurance Criteria, direct evidence assessment, determine adjudication or control the resulting Assurance Finding /\allowbreak{} Conclusion. REQ-FND-005 control independence remains applicable, including where a requester performs or manages the subject. Detailed payloads, contracts, initiation mechanics and states remain unresolved.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Service Overview: This Service gives approved requesting roles a governed way to seek assurance within their authority. A request expresses the legitimate assurance need; it does not confer control over criteria, evidence assessment or adjudication. The requester can be involved in the subject while the required independence of the conclusion remains intact.

elements.adjudication_note: HUMAN ADJUDICATION REQUIRED: Canonical assurance against a governed subject is not independent review of the assurance service itself.

elements.name: Request Service Assurance Status

sources.text: ### 5.2 Request Service Assurance Status

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Request Service Assurance Status}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Enables the System Steward to obtain the current business progression state of an identifiable Service Assurance activity for stewardship purposes.



\item 
\textbf{Only Approved Consumer}: \texttt{\seqsplit{System Steward}}.



\item 
\textbf{Associated Interaction}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md\#service-assurance-status}{Service Assurance Status}, between System Steward and Service Guardian.



\item 
\textbf{Status Boundary}: Concerns \textbf{activity progression state}. It does not communicate provisional findings, incomplete assessment results as conclusions, predicted outcomes or unadjudicated conclusions. Other requesting Roles do not gain status access merely because they requested assurance. No detailed activity-status taxonomy is established.



\end{itemize}

\textbf{Service Assurance Status answers "where is the assurance activity in its progression?" It does not answer "what has the assurance established?"} The latter requires an adjudicated Assurance Finding /\allowbreak{} Conclusion and subsequent outcome communication; neither status nor execution completion establishes that conclusion.


\textbf{Management Monitoring evaluates activity state in order to progress or manage activity. Assurance evaluates activity against governing criteria in order to establish an assurance conclusion.} System Steward's use of this Service is stewardship /\allowbreak{} management observation of assurance progression, not itself assurance or recursive assurance. The non-recursion boundary in §7.2 applies.

baseline_description.Service Overview: The status Service exposes progression of an identifiable assurance activity exclusively to System Steward. Its client question is where the activity has reached, not what the evidence will establish. Requesting assurance does not automatically grant status access, and progression observation is stewardship rather than recursive assurance.

sources.text: ### 5.3 Communicate Service Assurance Outcome

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Communicate Service Assurance Outcome}}.



\item 
\textbf{Definition}: Communicates applicable established Assurance Findings and Conclusions to authorised recipients according to their responsibilities, authority and information requirements.



\item 
\textbf{Approved Potential Recipients}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Care Coordinator}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{Service Coordinator}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{Regulator}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{Policy Authority}}, \texttt{\seqsplit{System Steward}}.



\item 
\textbf{Associated Interaction}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md\#service-assurance-outcome-communication}{Service Assurance Outcome Communication}, with Service Guardian and one or more authorised recipient Roles.



\item 
\textbf{Process Relationship}: Exposes the communication behaviour of \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/processes/business-processes.md\#assurance-process-reporting-communication}{Assurance Process Reporting /\allowbreak{} Communication}, beginning from an already established finding/\allowbreak{}conclusion. It does not perform assessment or adjudication or alter/\allowbreak{}reinterpret the established outcome. A documentary report is not required.



\item 
\textbf{Recipient Boundary}: No mandatory broadcast is established. A particular outcome may be communicated to one, some or all legitimate recipients according to applicability, authority, responsibility and information requirements. Requester, status consumer and outcome recipient need not be the same Role. Communication does not transfer responsibility for recipients' interpretation within their authority, operational/\allowbreak{}clinical management, remediation, escalation, policy/\allowbreak{}compliance response, process improvement or other subsequent action to Service Guardian.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Service Overview: Outcome communication exposes already established findings to applicable authorised recipients from the approved roles. It preserves the adjudicated meaning and does not require a broadcast to every possible recipient. Receipt does not transfer the recipient's subsequent clinical, governance or operational action to Service Guardian.

elements.name: Governed Person Identity Correction Process

sources.text: ### 2.1 Governed Person Identity Correction Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Person Identity` (under `Client Administration`)

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Person Identity}} (under \texttt{\seqsplit{Client Administration}})



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Processes externally authoritative identity corrections and merge/\allowbreak{}unlink outcomes, applies their consequences to Harmonia-managed identity information and identifier associations, and communicates resulting changes with an audit history.



\item 
\textbf{Authority boundary}: Person correction/\allowbreak{}merge decisions originate externally. Internal triage, evidence verification and approval concern applicability and governed processing of that authoritative outcome, not person matching, golden-record determination, master-person selection or originating merge adjudication.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Correction Requested → HIM Triage → Evidence Verified → Correction Approved → Merge/\allowbreak{}Unlink Executed → Change Broadcasted → Closed



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Correction Requested}}: Externally authoritative correction or merge/\allowbreak{}unlink outcome received for governed application.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{HIM Triage}}: Health Information Manager reviews the received decision/\allowbreak{}outcome and its applicability.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Evidence Verified}}: Authoritative source decision and supporting provenance/\allowbreak{}documentation verified.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Correction Approved}}: Governed application of the externally authoritative outcome approved; this does not originate a person-merge decision.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Merge/Unlink Executed}}: External merge/\allowbreak{}unlink consequences applied to Harmonia's managed identifier associations and audit history.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Change Broadcasted}}: Downstream clinical systems notified of merged or rectified identity.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: This Process governs the application of an externally authoritative correction rather than originating a person-merge judgement. Triage, evidence verification and approval establish that the received outcome should be applied to Harmonia's associations. The progression and change communication preserve why the managed identity account changed without making internal approval a master-person decision.

elements.name: Practitioner Verification Process

sources.text: ### 2.2 Practitioner Verification Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Provider Administration`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Provider Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the lifecycle of validating, certifying, and periodically re-verifying a healthcare practitioner's professional credentials, registration status, and clinical scope of practice.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Verification Initiated → Regulatory Registry Queried → Credentials Validated → Privileges Endorsed → Active Verified → Expired /\allowbreak{} Suspended



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Verification Initiated}}: New practitioner registration or periodic re-credentialing triggered.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Regulatory Registry Queried}}: Real-time query executed against national registry (e.g., AHPRA).



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Credentials Validated}}: Primary qualifications, specialist endorsements, and sanctions checked.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Privileges Endorsed}}: Health service medical administration endorses admitting/\allowbreak{}procedural scope.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Active Verified}}: Practitioner verified for clinical ordering and electronic communication.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Expired / Suspended}}: Verification lapses or regulatory sanction triggers privilege suspension.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: Verification progresses from checking the recognised professional source to the locally applicable endorsement and continuing verification status. The distinction matters because a nationally identifiable practitioner is not automatically privileged for every service activity. The illustrated progression retains the health service's endorsement responsibility rather than letting directory ingestion grant clinical authority.

elements.name: Referral Progression Process

sources.text: ### 3.3 Referral Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Referral Administration`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Referral Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the end-to-end operational progression of an incoming clinical referral from receipt through specialist clinical triage, booking, and final service acceptance.



\item 
\textbf{Scope qualification}: This illustrates a specialist booking/\allowbreak{}attendance pathway; Referral does not universally require acceptance, scheduling, attendance or discharge, or establish delivery, responsibility actually assumed or Transfer of Care. Decline, rejection and redirection remain valid dispositions without invented transition paths. \texttt{\seqsplit{Accepted / Waitlisted}} is a local compound checkpoint, not universal equivalence between acceptance and waitlisting.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Submitted → Intake Validated → Clinically Triaged → Accepted /\allowbreak{} Waitlisted → Scheduled → Consultation Attended → Discharged /\allowbreak{} Rejected   (Illustrative specialist pathway; dispositions vary)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Submitted}}: Electronic referral received from GP or external facility.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Intake Validated}}: Administrative validation of patient details, mandatory fields, and tests.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Clinically Triaged}}: Senior clinician assigns urgency category (e.g., Cat 1 urgent within 30 days).



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Accepted / Waitlisted}}: Referral accepted and placed onto the specialty waitlist.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Scheduled}}: Outpatient appointment allocated and patient notified.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Consultation Attended}}: Patient seen; initial specialist assessment completed.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharged / Rejected}}: Referral completed and discharged back to primary care, or formally rejected with clinical rationale.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: This Process illustrates one specialist pathway through validation, triage and booking. It makes that pathway's progression visible without imposing it on every referral: rejection, decline or redirection can be legitimate dispositions, and a request need not universally lead to attendance. Neither a transmitted referral nor the local compound acceptance/waitlist checkpoint establishes actual responsibility transfer.

elements.name: Encounter Lifecycle Process

sources.text: ### 3.4 Encounter Lifecycle Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Episode & Encounter Administration`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Episode \& Encounter Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the clinical and administrative lifecycle of an acute, emergency, inpatient, or outpatient encounter between a patient and healthcare services.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Planned /\allowbreak{} Booked → Arrived → Triaged /\allowbreak{} Ingested → Active In-Progress → Discharged → Completed /\allowbreak{} Encoded   (Scoped illustration; ON\_LEAVE relationship unresolved)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Planned / Booked}}: Elective admission or clinic appointment scheduled.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Arrived}}: Patient presents at facility or emergency desk.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Triaged / Ingested}}: Clinical triage category assigned; encounter record activated.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Active In-Progress}}: Inpatient care, bedside monitoring, and clinical orders actively underway.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharged}}: Patient clinically discharged; care-place vacated.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Completed / Encoded}}: Clinical documentation finalized, ICD/\allowbreak{}DRG coding completed, and encounter legally closed.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Scope qualification}: These completion criteria retain their locally described applicability; they do not establish universal signing, legal closure or originating authority over clinical information. Finalisation, signing and legal qualification remain distinct. The relationship with Strategy \texttt{\seqsplit{ON\_LEAVE}}, including applicability and transitions, remains unresolved.



\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: The encounter lifecycle distinguishes the planned opportunity, presence, active encounter and locally applicable completion context. It supplies an administrative progression frame for care information rather than evidence that every clinical objective has been met. The relation to Strategy's ON_LEAVE state remains unresolved, and local signing or legal-closure descriptions do not become universal completion rules.

elements.name: Closed-Loop Order Progression Process

sources.text: ### 3.5 Closed-Loop Order Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Order Administration`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Order Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the rigorous, closed-loop tracking of diagnostic pathology, radiology, and procedural orders from requisition to result correlation, preventing dropped or unfulfilled investigations.



\item 
\textbf{Scope qualification}: These examples describe a diagnostic/\allowbreak{}procedural progression and do not exclude medication from the broader Order Administration responsibility. Specimen and result checkpoints are scoped. The signed requisition/\allowbreak{}report requirements remain within this illustrated scope; signing is not universally equivalent to finalisation or authority. Result consumption/\allowbreak{}binding does not define originating validity, authority, authorship or legal status.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Requisition Placed → Order Dispatched → Specimen Collected /\allowbreak{} Scheduled → In-Execution → Preliminary Result Bound → Final Result Bound → Closed /\allowbreak{} Verified   (Scoped diagnostic/\allowbreak{}procedural illustration)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Requisition Placed}}: Electronic order created and signed by requesting clinician.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Order Dispatched}}: Order routed and accepted by performing diagnostic service. This local compound checkpoint retains routing and recipient acceptance as distinct facts; dispatch alone establishes neither receipt nor acceptance. Behaviour \texttt{\seqsplit{Received}} is not equated with this checkpoint without evidence.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Collected / Scheduled}}: Bio-specimen collected or imaging appointment booked.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Execution}}: Laboratory analysis or diagnostic scanning underway.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Preliminary Result Bound}}: Critical or interim observations published and linked to order.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Final Result Bound}}: Authoritative diagnostic report signed and bound to order.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Closed / Verified}}: Requesting clinician acknowledges result; order closed. This Order-closure checkpoint does not establish diagnostic-content verification, approval or clinical incorporation.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: Closed-loop progression preserves the connection between the requisition, performing context and returned result so that a request does not disappear after dispatch. The diagnostic/procedural illustration includes specimen and report checkpoints without excluding medication from the broader owning capability. Dispatch, recipient acceptance, result binding and requester closure remain distinct facts even where a source checkpoint combines them.

elements.name: Clinical Document Lifecycle Process

sources.text: ### 3.6 Clinical Document Lifecycle Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Clinical Record Administration`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Record Administration}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the versioning, clinical sign-off, addenda, superseding, and legal status of clinical documents (discharge summaries, specialist letters, advance care directives).



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Draft → Preliminary → Final Signed → Amended /\allowbreak{} Addended → Superseded → Entered-in-Error   (Scoped illustration; no universal document lifecycle)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Draft}}: Incomplete clinical document saved during consultation.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Preliminary}}: Document authored pending senior registrar or consultant countersignature.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Final Signed}}: Authoritative clinical document legally signed and published.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Amended / Addended}}: Governed supplementary clinical addendum appended to signed document.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Superseded}}: Entire document replaced by a newer revision; prior version retained for audit.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Entered-in-Error}}: Document formally retracted due to wrong patient or invalid content; content struck through with retraction notice.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Scope qualification}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Final ≠ automatically Final Signed}}. The described signing/\allowbreak{}countersigning and legal qualifications remain local requirements, not a universal document lifecycle. Authorship, attestation, approval, authentication, verification, signature, finalisation, authority and legal qualification remain distinct. Amendment, supersession and entered-in-error are not mandatory stages for every document, and consumer processing does not establish originating authority or legal status.



\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: This Process makes authorship and changing document standing intelligible through the locally described review, amendment and withdrawal circumstances. It preserves prior versions rather than treating correction as erasure. The illustration does not require every document to pass through every stage or make finalisation, signing, legal qualification and originating authority equivalent.

elements.name: Theatre Case Progression Process

sources.text: ### 4.7 Theatre Case Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Theatre Operations`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Theatre Operations}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the perioperative operational milestones of a surgical procedure within the operating theatre suite.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Case Called → In Anaesthetic Bay → Anaesthesia Commenced → Patient in Theatre → Knife-to-Skin → Procedure Finished → In PACU Recovery → Ward Handover Complete



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Case Called}}: Theatre team requests ward to send patient for surgery.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In Anaesthetic Bay}}: Patient arrives in theatre holding and identity/\allowbreak{}consent verified.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Anaesthesia Commenced}}: Anaesthetic induction underway.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Patient in Theatre}}: Patient transferred onto operating table.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Knife-to-Skin}}: Surgical incision initiated (operative start).



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Procedure Finished}}: Wound closure completed and dressings applied.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In PACU Recovery}}: Patient monitored in post-anaesthesia care unit.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Ward Handover Complete}}: Post-operative clinical handover to inpatient ward completed.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: Theatre case progression follows reported milestones of the surgical encounter so that supporting participants can coordinate around the actual situation. The state account concerns what the clinical service reports has occurred. It does not make the integration mechanism the actor administering anaesthesia, performing surgery or managing clinical handover.

elements.name: Clinic / Operational Queue Progression Process

sources.text: ### 4.8 Clinic / Operational Queue Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Clinic & Practice Operations`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Clinic \& Practice Operations}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the movement and state tracking of outpatients through an ambulatory specialty clinic session.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Scheduled → Patient Arrived → Checked-In → Roomed /\allowbreak{} Pre-Consult → Consultation In-Progress → Consultation Concluded → Departed



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Scheduled}}: Appointment booked on session list.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Patient Arrived}}: Patient enters waiting area.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Checked-In}}: Reception verifies demographics and marks patient ready.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Roomed / Pre-Consult}}: Nursing staff record baseline vitals and room patient.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Consultation In-Progress}}: Clinician actively conducting consultation.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Consultation Concluded}}: Clinical discussion finished; follow-up orders placed.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Departed}}: Patient checks out and departs clinic facility.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: This Process follows an individual's operational passage through the clinic. Waiting, rooming, consultation and departure have different implications for flow and communication, while the clinic's overall session has its own state. The progression is therefore patient-specific operational context rather than a complete account of clinic capacity or clinical priority.

elements.name: Bed Turnover Process

sources.text: ### 4.9 Bed Turnover Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Bed & Care-Place Management`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Bed \& Care-Place Management}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the rapid physical turnover, cleaning, sanitisation, and re-allocation of inpatient and emergency care-places.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Bed Vacated → Cleaning Dispatched → Sanitisation In-Progress → Terminal Cleaning Verified → Bed Ready /\allowbreak{} Available → Bed Allocated /\allowbreak{} Occupied



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Bed Vacated}}: Prior patient discharged or transferred.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Cleaning Dispatched}}: Cleaning job allocated to environmental services team.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Sanitisation In-Progress}}: Ward cleaning or isolation decontamination underway.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Terminal Cleaning Verified}}: Ward coordinator or supervisor verifies care-place readiness.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Bed Ready / Available}}: Bed marked available for incoming patient allocation.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Bed Allocated / Occupied}}: Incoming patient allocated and physically placed in bed.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: Bed turnover connects the release of a care place with the operational work needed to return it to use. Its progression preserves the difference between vacancy, cleaning and readiness. A place can be empty while work remains outstanding, and a completed turnover does not by itself prove that the service has capacity for the next patient.

elements.name: Operational Work Progression Process

sources.text: ### 4.10 Operational Work Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Work Allocation & Dispatch`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Work Allocation \& Dispatch}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the dispatch, assignment, execution, and completion of facility operational jobs (e.g., equipment moves, waste removal, linen supply).



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Work Requested → Queued in Dispatch → Assigned to Worker → Job Accepted → Work In-Progress → Work Completed /\allowbreak{} Aborted



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Work Requested}}: Facility support task submitted by clinical unit.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Queued in Dispatch}}: Job prioritized in operational queue.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Assigned to Worker}}: Job allocated to specific staff member or team.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Job Accepted}}: Worker acknowledges dispatch on mobile device.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Work In-Progress}}: Task actively being executed.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Work Completed / Aborted}}: Job marked finished or formally cancelled with reason.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: Operational work progression makes the path from a recognised support requirement to assigned and reported work explicit. Acknowledgement and activity progress help distinguish a dispatch from actual performance and expose impediments requiring operational attention. This responsibility remains bounded to authorised support work rather than ownership of the clinician's worklist.

elements.name: Patient Transport Process

sources.text: ### 4.11 Patient Transport Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Patient Transport`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Patient Transport}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the physical portering and transport of patients between hospital departments, wards, diagnostic suites, and external facilities.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Transport Requested → Porter Dispatched → Patient Collected → In-Transit → Delivered at Destination → Clinical Handover Complete



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Transport Requested}}: Clinical unit books wheelchair, bed, or ambulance transport.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Porter Dispatched}}: Wardsperson assigned and en route to pickup location.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Patient Collected}}: Patient identity verified and transfer initiated.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Transit}}: Patient actively moving through facility corridors or ambulance transit.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Delivered at Destination}}: Patient arrives at target diagnostic suite or ward.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Handover Complete}}: Safe custody and clinical briefing transferred to receiving staff.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: Patient transport progression records the physical journey from a movement request through departure, transit and destination arrival. Its checkpoints allow operational participants to follow the journey with relevant mobility context intact. Arrival closes a movement concern only under its applicable scope; it does not establish clinical handover or destination acceptance of care responsibility.

elements.name: Specimen Transport Process

sources.text: ### 4.12 Specimen Transport Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Clinical Logistics Coordination`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Logistics Coordination}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the physical courier chain-of-custody, transport, and delivery of pathology bio-specimens, blood products, and surgical biopsies.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Specimen Packaged → Courier Dispatched → Chain-of-Custody Signed → In-Transit (Monitored) → Lab Ingress Received → Specimen Accepted



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Packaged}}: Clinical unit packages bio-sample with barcode manifest.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Courier Dispatched}}: Courier route assigned for pickup.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Chain-of-Custody Signed}}: Courier scans barcode and accepts legal custody.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Transit (Monitored)}}: Specimen in transit under temperature/\allowbreak{}time constraints.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Lab Ingress Received}}: Central pathology specimen reception logs physical receipt.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Specimen Accepted}}: Specimen integrity verified and passed to analytical track.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: Specimen transport preserves the movement and custody account connecting collection context with laboratory receipt. It makes the journey of the material explainable rather than reducing it to a sent/received pair. Delivery remains distinct from specimen acceptance, diagnostic performance and the eventual professional interpretation of its evidence.

elements.name: Discharge Progression Process

sources.text: ### 4.13 Discharge Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Discharge Management`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Management}}



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Governs the multidisciplinary coordination of patient discharge planning, pharmacy reconciliation, transport, and community handover.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Discharge Planning Initiated → Clinical Readiness Confirmed → Medications Reconciled → Transport \& Services Booked → Discharge Summary Signed → Physically Departed   (Illustrative preparation; publication, authorisation and exit distinct)



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Planning Initiated}}: Estimated Date of Discharge (EDD) set on admission.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Clinical Readiness Confirmed}}: Attending medical team declares patient fit for discharge.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Medications Reconciled}}: Hospital pharmacy reconciles and dispenses discharge medications.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Transport \& Services Booked}}: Community nursing, home equipment, and patient transport booked.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Discharge Summary Signed}}: Applicable signed summary is available/\allowbreak{}published and may be communicated before departure where the Business behaviour requires it; signing, finalisation, publication and discharge authorisation remain distinct.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Physically Departed}}: Confirmed physical exit triggers departure notifications, updated bed-state communication and finalised-summary dispatch to external care providers under \texttt{\seqsplit{FEAT-HSO-29}}; care-place turnover follows its own responsibility.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Timing reconciliation}: Preparation, information availability/\allowbreak{}publication, applicable discharge authorisation and physical exit are distinct. Earlier preparation/\allowbreak{}communication is permitted; it does not realise a Feature triggered by confirmed exit. This illustrated local pathway establishes neither universal publication timing nor a universal discharge state machine, and adds no inferred publication event or authorisation state.



\item 
\textbf{Preserved uncertainty}: Summary signing and finalisation are not universal equivalents. Detailed applicability, discharge-authority workflows and timing beyond the established preparation/\allowbreak{}confirmed-exit distinction remain unestablished.



\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: Discharge progression coordinates the confirmations and practical requirements around leaving care. Clinical readiness, medications, destination arrangements and transport are related but distinct contributions, and the source progression retains its stated local applicability. Operational coordination does not originate the clinical discharge decision or prove that another provider assumed responsibility.

sources.text: ### 5.14 Work Order Progression Process
- **Owning Capability**: `Workflow & Activity Coordination`

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Workflow \& Activity Coordination}}



\item 
\textbf{Activity Archetype}: \textbf{Human Doing} — physical or operational task executed by healthcare staff.



\item 
\textbf{State Progression Lifecycle}: Created → Ready → Dispatched → Accepted → In-Progress → Completed /\allowbreak{} Failed /\allowbreak{} Cancelled



\item 
\textbf{Key State Dispositions}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Created}}: Work order instantiated with scope, target, and required skills.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Ready}}: Preconditions satisfied; available for assignment.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Dispatched}}: Sent to target individual or worker group queue.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Accepted}}: Worker claims task.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{In-Progress}}: Execution underway.



\item 
\texttt{\seqsplit{Completed}}: Task finished with recorded completion telemetry.



\end{itemize}


\end{itemize}

\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Process Overview: Work Order progression describes a human undertaking physical or operational activity. Assignment, acknowledgement and outcome make the undertaking accountable without collapsing dispatch into completion. Its generic work meaning can support different operational contexts while leaving their domain authority and the clinical-work boundary intact.

sources.text: ### 6.1 Assurance Process Design
- **Owning Capability**: [Assurance Design](../../02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#assurance-design).

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Assurance Process Design}}.



\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md\#assurance-design}{Assurance Design}.



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Establishes and maintains how satisfaction of a governed requirement, constraint or expected behaviour is to be assured.



\item 
\textbf{Principal Performing Role}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/actors-roles/roles.md\#service-assurance-modeller}{Service Assurance Modeller}.



\item 
\textbf{Participating Functions}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#design-service-assurance}{Design Service Assurance} and \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#manage-assurance-criteria}{Manage Assurance Criteria}. Manage Assurance Criteria retains ownership within Assurance Criteria Management; its participation does not subsume that Capability's criteria lifecycle or transfer its information responsibility to Assurance Design.



\item 
\textbf{Conceptual Output}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#42-assurance-definition--conceptual-modelling-output}{Assurance Definition}, retaining its conceptual Business Architecture output/\allowbreak{}boundary treatment.



\item 
\textbf{Boundary}: Governance Authority establishes what is authoritative. Design does not grant Service Assurance Modeller approval authority. Detailed Assurance Definition lifecycle, approval/\allowbreak{}publication workflows, criteria lifecycle and information modelling remain unresolved. Participation of the two Functions does not establish a cross-capability lifecycle or a new exchange/\allowbreak{}Service between their owners.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Process Overview: Assurance design establishes a reusable basis for how satisfaction will be evaluated, rather than running the evaluation itself. Criteria-management participation retains its separate owner and does not create an exchange Service or a shared criteria lifecycle. An Assurance Definition can be reused, so each execution need not imply a freshly performed Design Process.

sources.text: ### 6.2 Assurance Process Execution
- **Owning Capability**: [Governed Assurance](../../02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#governed-assurance).

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize} \item \textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Assurance Process Execution}}. \item \textbf{Owning Capability}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md\#governed-assurance}{Governed Assurance}. \item \textbf{Process Purpose}: Performs defined assurance for an identifiable governed subject in accordance with an applicable Assurance Definition and establishes an Assurance Finding /\allowbreak{} Conclusion from applicable trustworthy evidence. \item \textbf{Principal Performing Role}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/actors-roles/roles.md\#service-guardian}{Service Guardian}. \item \textbf{Participating Functions}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#establish-assurance-context}{Establish Assurance Context}, \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#assess-assurance-evidence}{Assess Assurance Evidence} and \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#adjudicate-assurance-assessment}{Adjudicate Assurance Assessment}, all retaining Governed Assurance ownership. \item \textbf{Conceptual Basis and Output}: Applicable Assurance Definition plus identifiable governed subject; Assurance Finding /\allowbreak{} Conclusion established through adjudication where sufficient trustworthy evidence permits. Correct execution with insufficient evidence does not imply satisfaction or non-satisfaction or force a conclusion. \item \textbf{Boundary}: Function completion does not define Process lifecycle states. No Context Established, Evidence Assessed, Adjudicated or Concluded states are inferred. Detailed lifecycle states, transitions and initiation mechanics remain unresolved. Requesting this Process does not grant control of evidence assessment, adjudication or the resulting finding/\allowbreak{}conclusion. \end{itemize} \textit{RAD diagram: textual source notation.} \begin{Verbatim}[breaklines,fontsize=\footnotesize] graph TD DEF["Applicable Assurance Definition
Conceptual basis"] -->|Assurance basis| EXEC["PR: Assurance Process Execution
Owner: Governed Assurance"] SUBJECT["Identifiable Governed Subject"] -->|Subject of assurance| EXEC EXEC -->|Participating Function| CONTEXT["FN: Establish Assurance Context"] EXEC -->|Participating Function| ASSESS["FN: Assess Assurance Evidence"] EXEC -->|Participating Function| ADJ["FN: Adjudicate Assurance Assessment"] EXEC -->|Establishes through adjudication| FINDING["Assurance Finding / Conclusion"] \end{Verbatim}

Correct execution with insufficient evidence remains different from execution failure and from a positive or negative conclusion about the subject. Participating Functions describe responsibilities without supplying unapproved lifecycle states.

sources.text: ### 6.3 Assurance Process Reporting / Communication
- **Owning Capability**: [Governed Assurance](../../02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#governed-assurance).

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Assurance Process Reporting / Communication}}.



\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md\#governed-assurance}{Governed Assurance}.



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Communicates applicable established Assurance Findings and Conclusions to legitimate recipients according to their responsibilities, authority and information requirements, without altering the established assurance outcome or assuming responsibility for the recipient's subsequent action.



\item 
\textbf{Starting Basis}: An already established Assurance Finding /\allowbreak{} Conclusion. This Process does not perform assessment or adjudication, alter or reinterpret the established outcome.



\item 
\textbf{Communication Participation}: Service Guardian participates through \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md\#service-assurance-outcome-communication}{Service Assurance Outcome Communication}, associated with \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#communicate-service-assurance-outcome}{Communicate Service Assurance Outcome}. No additional Function is introduced to populate this Process.



\item 
\textbf{Boundary}: Reporting /\allowbreak{} Communication is not limited to documentary report production; an appropriate Business Interaction may communicate the outcome without a report document. It assumes no operational response, remediation, escalation, policy/\allowbreak{}compliance response, process improvement, clinical management, clinical judgement or other recipient action. Detailed communication progression and completion semantics remain unresolved.



\end{itemize}

Communication need not create a report document, and it does not repeat assessment or adjudication. - **Owning Capability**: [Governed Assurance](../../02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md#governed-assurance).

pre_review_record.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Canonical Name}: \texttt{\seqsplit{Assurance Process Reporting / Communication}}.



\item 
\textbf{Owning Capability}: \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md\#governed-assurance}{Governed Assurance}.



\item 
\textbf{Process Purpose}: Communicates applicable established Assurance Findings and Conclusions to legitimate recipients according to their responsibilities, authority and information requirements, without altering the established assurance outcome or assuming responsibility for the recipient's subsequent action.



\item 
\textbf{Starting Basis}: An already established Assurance Finding /\allowbreak{} Conclusion. This Process does not perform assessment or adjudication, alter or reinterpret the established outcome.



\item 
\textbf{Communication Participation}: Service Guardian participates through \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/collaborations-interactions/interactions.md\#service-assurance-outcome-communication}{Service Assurance Outcome Communication}, associated with \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/03-business-architecture/behaviours/health-service-assurance.md\#communicate-service-assurance-outcome}{Communicate Service Assurance Outcome}. No additional Function is introduced to populate this Process.



\item 
\textbf{Boundary}: Reporting /\allowbreak{} Communication is not limited to documentary report production; an appropriate Business Interaction may communicate the outcome without a report document. It assumes no operational response, remediation, escalation, policy/\allowbreak{}compliance response, process improvement, clinical management, clinical judgement or other recipient action. Detailed communication progression and completion semantics remain unresolved.



\end{itemize}

Communication need not create a report document, and it does not repeat assessment or adjudication. Recipients retain authority and responsibility for any clinical, operational, policy or improvement action they take in response.

elements.name: Managed Entity & Relationship

sources.text: ### EC-01: Managed Entity & Relationship

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Identify, classify, relate, and maintain the structural integrity of managed healthcare and administrative entities throughout the enterprise landscape.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Uniquely identifying core domain entities (Persons, Practitioners, Roles, Organisations, Locations, Services, Devices).



\item 
Resolving and maintaining multi-authority identifier systems and aliases without destructive overwriting.



\item 
Representing and traversing multi-dimensional relationships (affiliations, organizational hierarchies, physical location trees, care team memberships).



\item 
Maintaining referential integrity across interconnected entity graphs.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not own physical database relational tables or foreign key constraints (Domain 04/\allowbreak{}07).



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Capability Overview: This reusable capability keeps managed healthcare entities identifiable and their relationships structurally intelligible. It supplies common identity, alias and relationship behaviour recurring in persons, practitioners, organisations, locations and devices. Reuse concerns those architectural responsibilities, allowing the healthcare-specific meaning of each entity to remain with its governing context.
baseline_description.Boundary: Relationship integrity is not a physical database design. Correlating entities does not establish originating clinical identity authority or a new standalone Correlation capability.

elements.name: Context Management

sources.text: ### EC-02: Context Management

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Establish, validate, propagate, and preserve the execution, clinical, security, and administrative context within which information and activities have meaning.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Binding the subject of care, encounter, ordering provider, and healthcare service context to in-flight messages and transactions.



\item 
Propagating tamper-evident, attributable security context across asynchronous, multi-hop operational boundaries.



\item 
Ensuring context preservation during cross-protocol transformations across disparate healthcare exchange formats and protocols.



\item 
Detecting and rejecting requests where mandatory operational or clinical context is missing or inconsistent.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Bounded reusable context responsibility may be realised through participation across gateways, activity execution and information-access boundaries. Participation does not transfer semantic ownership.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Capability Overview: Context Management preserves the circumstances in which information and activity have meaning as they cross processing boundaries. Subject, encounter, provider, service and security context must remain attributable and consistent rather than be reconstructed from convenient local assumptions. Its reuse is especially significant in multi-hop activity where a syntactically valid message can otherwise lose the context required for legitimate interpretation.
baseline_description.Boundary: Context participation does not transfer semantic ownership. Generic context management and assurance-specific context semantics contribute together without allocating a new central Context Service.

elements.name: Managed State & Lifecycle

sources.text: ### EC-03: Managed State & Lifecycle

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Govern the current and historical state, effective temporal periods, state transition validations, and lifecycle progression of managed integration artifacts and entities.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Defining and enforcing valid state transition state machines (e.g., \texttt{\seqsplit{REQUESTED}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{VALIDATED}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{IN\_PROGRESS}} → \texttt{\seqsplit{COMPLETED}}).



\item 
Maintaining temporal validity intervals (effective start and end dates) for relationships, credentials, and states.



\item 
Supporting non-destructive state progression, preserving historical state versions for longitudinal review.



\item 
Rejecting illegal or out-of-order state transitions while accommodating idempotent replay.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not define thread-level mutexes or database transaction isolation levels.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Capability Overview: Managed State & Lifecycle provides reusable responsibility for valid progression, temporal applicability and non-destructive change. A directory relationship, clinical document and operational work item have different business states, yet all need an intelligible distinction between current standing, historical state and invalid transitions. The capability captures that recurrence without replacing each subject's lifecycle meaning.
baseline_description.Boundary: Business lifecycle integrity does not prescribe locks, database isolation or worker implementation, and illustrative state names do not define every subject's transitions.

elements.name: Information Management

sources.text: ### EC-04: Information Management

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Validate, represent, persist, retrieve, version, and manage governed clinical, administrative, and operational information assets.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Validating inbound information structures against canonical information constraints.



\item 
Providing authoritative durable persistence for historical health records and administrative registries.



\item 
Managing active distributed working memory representations for low-latency retrieval.



\item 
Governing document versioning, supersession, amendments, and retractions without data loss.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Architectural Principle}: Enforces the foundational separation between \emph{active distributed state access} and \emph{authoritative durable state preservation} (Axiom AX-05).



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Capability Overview: Information Management provides the recurring ability to represent and maintain governed information through validation, preservation, retrieval and versioned change. It accommodates both responsive active use and authoritative durable preservation while keeping those responsibilities separate. This distinction allows availability and working state to support care without turning a cache into durable truth.
baseline_description.Boundary: Engine capabilities provide machinery under Harmonia semantics. Persistence success does not establish information authority or make the platform the originator of the represented facts.
