elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Index, search, resolve, filter, and discover information assets, entities, directory endpoints, and healthcare services across the enterprise.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Providing multi-criteria indexed search across complex entity graphs (e.g., find active cardiologists at Location X accepting new referrals).



\item 
Resolving service and practitioner communication endpoints for addressed delivery.



\item 
Supporting bounded, paginated clinical queries across longitudinal patient records.



\item 
Applying dynamic security and consent filters to search results prior to egress.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not dictate specific search engine indexes, inverted index implementations, or SQL query syntaxes.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Capability Overview: Search & Discovery makes information, entities and service endpoints findable through governed criteria and bounded queries. It addresses the recurring need to locate relevant material or a destination before it can be used. Security-qualified results preserve the distinction between knowing that something exists and being entitled to obtain or disclose it.
baseline_description.Boundary: Discovery does not decide policy or prescribe a search engine, index format or query language.

sources.text: ### EC-06: Policy & Control

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Evaluate and enforce security, consent, privacy, and regulatory policies including authority, access control, and information handling rules.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Executing impartial, default-deny policy evaluations for all integration transactions.



\item 
Enforcing Role-Based and Attribute-Based Access Control (RBAC/\allowbreak{}ABAC) policies.



\item 
Evaluating patient consent directives and privacy restrictions at boundary and query checkpoints.



\item 
Enforcing statutory information disclosure boundaries (e.g., mental health, VIP records).



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Evaluated across boundary gateways, internal bus dispatch, storage interfaces, and presentation layers.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Capability Overview: Policy & Control supplies the reusable evaluation and enforcement of authority, consent, privacy and handling constraints. Its purpose is consistent governed action across ingress, information access, execution and presentation boundaries. Default-deny evaluation preserves the need for established authority rather than treating a caller's intent or a technically valid request as permission.
baseline_description.Boundary: Participation at multiple enforcement points does not distribute policy ownership or turn operational security context into persistent clinical content.

elements.name: Provenance & Traceability

sources.text: ### EC-07: Provenance & Traceability

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Preserve required origin attribution, meaningful transformation history, significant execution checkpoints, tamper-evident audit evidence and end-to-end traceability. Harmonia SHALL preserve provenance, audit and operational evidence where required by governing obligations, architectural significance, accountability, reconstruction, security or assurance needs. Routine technical activity SHALL NOT automatically require durable evidentiary recording.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Recording attributable, verifiable origin metadata for information sources, authors, and timestamps.



\item 
Tracking information-significant transformation history and required mapping checkpoints as information crosses system seams.



\item 
Capturing non-PHI operational and security audit trails for regulatory compliance (HIPAA, GDPR).



\item 
Supporting end-to-end transaction tracing across asynchronous processing pipelines.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Participating elements preserve required provenance and audit context according to policy. Telemetry, operational facts, provenance, audit and assurance evidence remain distinct. Being evidence is contextual, not an intrinsic property of every recorded fact; preservation does not establish an assurance conclusion.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Capability Overview: Provenance & Traceability preserves the meaningful attribution and history needed to explain information and significant activity. It connects source, transformation and required checkpoints without making every internal mechanism permanent evidence. Its recurring contribution supports accountability, reconstruction and assurance use while retaining the context that makes a recorded fact evidentially relevant.
baseline_description.Boundary: Telemetry, provenance, audit and assurance evidence remain distinct. Recording evidence neither establishes an assurance conclusion nor automatically requires retention of routine technical activity.

sources.text: ### EC-08: Interoperability & Exchange

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Resolve destinations, transform schemas, route, transport, deliver, acknowledge, and coordinate standards-based information exchange across enterprise boundaries.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Providing multi-protocol boundary adaptation for healthcare standards (HL7 v2, FHIR REST, DICOM, secure messaging).



\item 
Executing bidirectional structural and semantic transformations between legacy formats and canonical representations.



\item 
Ensuring reliable addressed delivery and fan-out distribution to external clinical endpoints.



\item 
Processing and distinguishing technical delivery acknowledgements from business acknowledgements.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Boundary Rule}: Egress terminates Harmonia management of the emitted representation (Axiom AX-13).



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Capability Overview: Interoperability & Exchange moves information across participating boundaries through destination resolution, transformation, delivery and acknowledgements. It preserves the difference between technical transmission and the recipient's business response so that an exchange can be understood under its actual contract. Standards govern the external representation while internal management semantics remain private.
baseline_description.Boundary: Egress ends Harmonia management of the emitted representation. Retained delivery evidence does not extend control over an external recipient or transfer payload authority.

sources.text: ### EC-09: Event & Subscription

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Publish, ingest, correlate, filter, and syndicate events and subscription-driven changes across the enterprise landscape.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Ingesting operational and clinical event triggers from external systems and internal state changes.



\item 
Managing topic- and criteria-based event subscriptions for internal and external consumers.



\item 
Evaluating dynamic subscription filters to match event payloads with interested subscriber criteria.



\item 
Delivering asynchronous event notifications reliably to registered subscribers.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Decoupling Note}: Defined strictly in terms of event publishing, criteria matching, and notification delivery; entirely independent of broker topics, partitions, or queues.



\end{itemize}

baseline_description.Capability Overview: Event & Subscription connects significant changes with participants whose registered interests match them. It makes event ingestion, correlation, interest criteria and notification reusable across clinical and operational contexts. The architectural meaning is the relationship between a change and an interested consumer, rather than the broker constructs used to carry it.
baseline_description.Boundary: Receiving a notification does not determine the consumer's business response; topics and queues do not define the capability.

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item

Instantiating operational work items (Work Orders, To Dos, synthetic platform Tasks) in response to triggers.

Matching and assigning work units to eligible human or automated performers and roles based on policy rules.



\item 
Dispatching work units to their assigned performers with acknowledgement according to the applicable interaction contract.



\item 
Supervising execution progress, tracking timeouts, managing escalations, and handling activity interruptions.



\end{itemize}


\item

elements.name: Operational Assurance

sources.text: ### EC-12: Operational Assurance

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Ensure concurrency integrity, system resilience, duplicate detection, exception handling, automated recovery, and operational telemetry across platform operations.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Enforcing sliding-window duplicate message detection and idempotent suppression.



\item 
Guaranteeing ingress dual-write safety (durable acceptance before emitting positive application ACK).



\item 
Managing structured failure recovery, exception escalation, and dead-letter isolation.



\item 
Emitting platform telemetry, operational health metrics, and queue processing metrics.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Realized collaboratively across boundary gateways, messaging infrastructure, execution workers, and storage layers.



\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{EC-12 /\allowbreak{} EC-14 Boundary}

EC-12 retains the established scope and responsibilities above. It may contribute directly to generic operational/\allowbreak{}processing assurance, limited to that contribution in the \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capability-maps/health-service-assurance-derivation.md\#collaborative-enterprise-capability-contribution-matrix}{approved assurance matrix}. It does not own the general semantics of assurance disposition, assurance-specific criteria applicability, evidentiary association, assessment against assurance criteria, adjudication, or independent assurance findings and conclusions. Those distinguishing responsibilities are introduced through EC-14 Service Guardian. Operational health and business-level processing assurance remain distinct; EC-12 is not expanded to absorb EC-14.

baseline_description.Capability Overview: Operational Assurance preserves processing integrity under concurrency, duplicate delivery and failure. It brings together resilience, durable ingress acceptance, recovery and operational telemetry so that technical degradation does not silently weaken the managed operation's semantics. Its contribution is collaborative across operational boundaries while remaining a bounded architectural responsibility.
baseline_description.Boundary: Operational health is distinct from independent assessment of a governed subject. Assurance-specific criteria applicability, adjudication and conclusions belong to the established EC-14 contribution.

\item 
Defining and publishing canonical healthcare data models and profile structures.

Governing clinical terminology mappings, value sets, and concept lookups (SNOMED CT, LOINC).

A conformant representation can therefore be distinguished from one that merely uses a supported transport or parser.

elements.name: Service Guardian

sources.text: ### EC-14: Service Guardian

elements.governed_definition_latex:
\begin{itemize}

\item 
\textbf{Architectural Scope}: Service Guardian provides the reusable capability to independently establish whether governed service behaviour, state or outcomes remain within defined assurance expectations by associating applicable criteria and trustworthy evidence with a governed subject, assessing that evidence, adjudicating the assessment, and establishing reportable assurance findings and conclusions.



\item 
\textbf{Functional Responsibilities}:


\begin{itemize}

\item 
Supplying assurance-specific semantics for assurance disposition and assurance criteria applicability.



\item 
Associating a governed subject/\allowbreak{}context with applicable criteria and sufficient trustworthy evidence for a particular assurance purpose.



\item 
Assessing evidence against applicable criteria and adjudicating assessed detail to establish reportable findings, exceptions and conclusions.



\item 
Preserving assurance independence, temporal/\allowbreak{}version-specific evidence and criteria applicability, and explicit inability to establish a conclusion where evidence is insufficient.



\end{itemize}


\item 
\textbf{Collaborative Nature}: Supplies the assurance-specific semantics required to bind existing reusable capabilities into governed assurance. It contributes directly to Assurance Design, Assurance Criteria Management and Governed Assurance; direct contribution is not sole realisation. The \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capability-maps/health-service-assurance-derivation.md\#collaborative-enterprise-capability-contribution-matrix}{approved matrix} preserves the contributions of EC-01 through EC-13.



\item 
\textbf{Anti-Responsibilities}: Does not own the underlying governed subject, authoritative governance requirements, or source information used as evidence. Does not perform, manage, remediate, assign, delegate or operationally escalate the subject activity. Does not replace System Operations or EC-12 Operational Assurance, and does not provide Clinical Services Delivery Assurance.



\item 
\textbf{Allocation Boundary}: No strategic logical component, application component, runtime service or implementation construct is allocated EC-14. The catalogue defines a capability, not a software component or deployment boundary.



\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Conceptual Behavioural Sequence}

\textit{RAD source listing (presentation only; no inferred ancestry).}
\begin{quote}
Define Good Behaviour

↓

Gather Evidence

↓

Assess Evidence against Good Behaviour

↓

Adjudicate Assessed Detail

↓

Report
\end{quote}

This sequence explains the capability; it is not an implementation workflow specification or a derived Business Process. “Define Good Behaviour” identifies assurance expectations and criteria; it does not transfer ownership of governing requirements to Service Guardian. Source information ownership remains with its responsible capability; assurance owns its contextual evidentiary association.


The \href{https://github.com/fhirfactory/harmonia/blob/98410db60155198a75f74c79d98060070209faa1/docs/markdown/02-strategy/capabilities/business-enabling-capabilities.md\#health-service-assurance-approved-business-enabling-capabilities}{Business Enabling assurance principles} govern disposition, generic processing assurance, evidence/\allowbreak{}criteria temporality, assessment/\allowbreak{}adjudication, independence, failure/\allowbreak{}recovery and explicit evidence insufficiency. These semantics are not universally reducible to PASS /\allowbreak{} FAIL /\allowbreak{} UNKNOWN and do not imply an assurance information model or persistence mechanism.


\par\smallskip

baseline_description.Capability Overview:
Service Guardian supplies the reusable assurance semantics that bind a governed subject to applicable criteria and trustworthy evidence, support assessment and adjudication, and establish reportable findings. Its contribution distinguishes explicit evidence insufficiency from a conclusion about the subject. Existing Enterprise Capabilities contribute collaboratively; EC-14 does not duplicate all their information, policy or execution responsibilities.

Independence concerns control of evaluation and conclusion. A subject may supply evidence but cannot solely determine, suppress or retrospectively change its own assurance outcome.
baseline_description.Boundary: The capability does not manage or remediate the subject, replace operational assurance, or assure clinical adequacy. No application component, runtime service or deployment boundary is allocated, and the explanatory sequence is not a derived Business Process.

- *Function*: `Resolve Person Identifier` — Validates and retrieves the authoritative demographic record bound to a specific identifier.
- *Exposed Service*: `Person Identifier Resolution` — Exposed to Service Administration and Service Delivery to disambiguate client identities.

- *Function*: `Correlate Person Identifiers` — Correlates local identifiers (e.g., Hospital MRN, National IHI, Pathology ID) using relationships established by authoritative information, retaining their source and namespace.
- *Exposed Service*: `Person Identifier Correlation` — Exposed across the HIE to establish patient cross-reference mappings.
- *Function*: `Maintain Person Identity Aliases` — Records and qualifies alias names, titles, and emergency aliases for a governed person identity.

- *Function*: `Apply Governed Person Identity Correction` — Processes externally authoritative corrections and merge/unlink outcomes, updates governed identity associations and propagates resulting managed-state consequences with audit history. Harmonia does not adjudicate the originating person-merge decision.
- *Exposed Service*: `Person Identity Correction` — Exposed to authorized HIM/Medical Records administrators.
- *Function*: `Establish Healthcare Subject Context` — Binds demographic, cultural, and communication requirements to a patient record.
- *Exposed Service*: `Healthcare Subject Context Resolution` — Provides comprehensive demographic, language, and indigenous status context to clinical applications.
- *Function*: `Govern Subject Demographic Context` — Applies validation rules to address changes, date of birth verification, and death notifications.
- *Exposed Service*: `Demographic Change Distribution` — Emits governed subject demographic updates to subscribed clinical systems.
- *Function*: `Maintain Client Relationships` — Records links between patients and carers, next of kin, nominated representatives, and legal guardians.
- *Exposed Service*: `Client Relationship Query` — Discloses verified support network members and contact details to clinical teams.
- *Function*: `Govern Client Relationship Validity` — Verifies power-of-attorney documents, guardianship orders, and proxy validity periods.
- *Exposed Service*: `Representative Authority Verification` — Confirms legal decision-making authority for substitute consent.
- *Function*: `Evaluate Client Consent` — Evaluates patient opt-in, opt-out, and general information sharing preferences against proposed exchanges.
- *Exposed Service*: `Consent Decision Service` — Provides real-time consent evaluation decisions to Health Information Control.
- *Function*: `Evaluate Client Confidentiality Restrictions` — Evaluates sensitive record flags (e.g., VIP masking, restricted department exclusions).
- *Exposed Service*: `Confidentiality Restriction Evaluation` — Enforces record-level masking directives across the HIE.
- *Function*: `Verify Practitioner Registration` — Validates national registration, specialty endorsements, and disciplinary sanctions against regulatory registries (e.g., AHPRA).
- *Exposed Service*: `Practitioner Verification Service` — Discloses verified registration and status to credentialing and clinical systems.
- *Function*: `Govern Practitioner Profile` — Maintains official names, professional identifiers (e.g., HPI-I, Prescriber Number), and clinical qualifications.
- *Exposed Service*: `Practitioner Directory Query` — Provides provider directory lookups across the healthcare network.
- *Function*: `Maintain Practitioner Roles` — Assigns and maintains clinical roles (e.g., Specialist Physician, Registrar, General Practitioner) fulfilled by a practitioner.
- *Exposed Service*: `Practitioner Role Resolution` — Resolves the specific clinical capacities of a practitioner.
- *Function*: `Bind Practitioner Electronic Endpoints` — Associates secure messaging addresses, direct communication endpoints, and notification preferences to practitioner roles.
- *Exposed Service*: `Practitioner Endpoint Lookup` — Provides secure message routing destinations for clinical communication.
- *Function*: `Maintain Practitioner Affiliations` — Tracks employment, admitting rights, and consulting appointments at specific healthcare facilities.
- *Exposed Service*: `Practitioner Affiliation Resolution` — Discloses organizational ties and practice locations.
- *Function*: `Maintain Clinical Privileges` — Records approved clinical scopes of practice, procedural authorizations, and prescribing privileges.
- *Exposed Service*: `Clinical Privilege Verification` — Verifies procedural and prescribing authority for clinical ordering systems.
- *Function*: `Verify Healthcare Organisation` — Validates enterprise legal identity, national facility identifiers (e.g., HPI-O), and accreditation status.
- *Exposed Service*: `Organisation Verification Service` — Provides verified organisation credentials to external and internal partners.
- *Function*: `Govern Organisation Profile` — Maintains official trading names, enterprise registration numbers, and governing bodies.
- *Exposed Service*: `Organisation Directory Query` — Discloses healthcare organisation profiles across the region.
- *Function*: `Maintain Organisational Structure` — Models parent-subsidiary relationships, clinical directorates, departments, and operational divisions.
- *Exposed Service*: `Organisational Hierarchy Resolution` — Resolves department nesting and reporting hierarchies.
- *Function*: `Maintain Organisation Contacts` — Manages administrative, clinical, and emergency contact details for facilities.
- *Exposed Service*: `Organisation Contact Lookup` — Provides official operational contact details.
- *Function*: `Maintain Healthcare Location` — Records physical sites, campuses, outpatient clinics, and community health centres.
- *Exposed Service*: `Location Directory Query` — Exposes location profiles and geospatial addresses.

- *Function*: `Maintain Physical Location Hierarchy` — Models the nested structural containment tree: `Campus` $\to$ `Building` $\to$ `Floor` $\to$ `Ward/Suite` $\to$ `Room/Bay` $\to$ `Bed Care-Place`.
- *Exposed Service*: `Location Hierarchy Resolution` — Discloses physical containment and navigation paths for clinical facilities.

- *Function*: `Maintain Care-Place Definition` — Defines static bed bays, treatment chairs, surgical tables, and emergency resuscitation cubicles, including equipment capabilities and oxygen/telemetry infrastructure.
- *Exposed Service*: `Care-Place Specification Lookup` — Discloses care-place physical capabilities to Bed & Care-Place Management.

- *Function*: `Maintain Healthcare Service Definition` — Defines clinical service offerings (e.g., Cardiology Outpatient Clinic, MRI Imaging, Acute Stroke Care), specialty classifications, and clinical scope.
- *Exposed Service*: `Healthcare Service Directory Query` — Exposes published clinical service offerings.
- *Function*: `Maintain Service / Location / Provider Map` — Binds health service definitions to delivering organisations, physical clinic locations, and participating practitioner roles.
- *Exposed Service*: `Service Provision Resolution` — Exposes multi-dimensional resolution queries answering who, where, and when healthcare services are delivered.
- *Function*: `Maintain Service Availability` — Governs regular operating hours, emergency intake availability, and seasonal clinic schedules.
- *Exposed Service*: `Service Availability Query` — Discloses operational intake hours and open status.
- *Function*: `Maintain Service Eligibility Rules` — Configures catchment criteria, age thresholds, referral requirements, and clinical indications for service access.
- *Exposed Service*: `Service Eligibility Evaluation` — Evaluates referral eligibility for intake coordinators.
- *Function*: `Maintain Device Definition` — Models medical device models, manufacturers, regulatory classifications (e.g., TGA/FDA classes), and calibration specifications.
- *Exposed Service*: `Device Definition Query` — Discloses approved medical device models and technical parameters.
- *Function*: `Maintain Device Instance Identity` — Tracks physical serial numbers, Unique Device Identifiers (UDI), asset tags, and firmware versions.
- *Exposed Service*: `Device Instance Resolution` — Resolves physical device instances from scanned barcodes or UDIs.
- *Function*: `Maintain Device Association` — Records active associations between clinical devices, patient encounters, and specific care-places (e.g., Bed 4 Vital Signs Monitor).
- *Exposed Service*: `Device Association Query` — Discloses active device-to-patient and device-to-location bindings.
- *Function*: `Maintain Device Communication Endpoints` — Manages network telemetry addresses, gateway ports, and protocol bindings for medical devices.
- *Exposed Service*: `Device Endpoint Resolution` — Exposes network addresses for telemetry routing.
- *Function*: `Receive Client Demographic Change` — Ingests administrative demographic updates from PAS/registration feeds.
- *Exposed Service*: `Demographic Intake Service` — Exposed to departmental registration systems.
- *Function*: `Distribute Governed Demographic Change` — Propagates verified demographic modifications to subscribed clinical subsystems.
- *Exposed Service*: `Demographic Update Notification` — Emits change notifications across the HIE.
- *Function*: `Receive Referral` — Validates and ingests structured electronic referrals, clinical indications, and priority categories.
- *Exposed Service*: `Referral Submission Service` — Exposed to external GP practices and referring health facilities.
- *Function*: `Assemble Referral Context` — Gathers relevant clinical history, medications, and diagnostic investigations into the referral package.
- *Exposed Service*: `Referral Context Query` — Provides comprehensive referral dossiers to intake triage clinicians.

- *Function*: `Manage Referral Progression` — Tracks referral disposition in an **illustrative specialist pathway; dispositions vary**: *Submitted* $\to$ *Triaged* $\to$ *Accepted/Waitlisted* $\to$ *Scheduled* $\to$ *Discharged*.
- *Exposed Service*: `Referral Status & Outcome Service` — Exposes progression milestones to referrers and patients.
- *Function*: `Receive Appointment Notification` — Ingests appointment creation, rescheduling, cancellation, and check-in events from host PAS engines.
- *Exposed Service*: `Appointment Notification Ingress` — Ingests booking events from departmental schedulers.
- *Function*: `Synchronise Appointment Status` — Projects synchronised appointment timelines to clinical dashboards and care coordinators.
- *Exposed Service*: `Appointment Schedule Query` — Exposes consolidated patient appointment schedules across facilities.
- *Function*: `Establish Encounter Context` — Binds patient, attending practitioner, clinical class (e.g., Inpatient, Emergency, Ambulatory), and admitting diagnosis to a unique encounter identifier.
- *Exposed Service*: `Encounter Context Resolution` — Discloses active encounter details to clinical applications.

- *Function*: `Progress Encounter State` — Coordinates encounter progression (**scoped illustration; ON_LEAVE relationship unresolved**): *Planned* $\to$ *Arrived* $\to$ *In-Progress* $\to$ *Discharged* $\to$ *Completed*.
- *Exposed Service*: `Encounter Lifecycle Event Notification` — Emits encounter transition events across the HIE.
- *Function*: `Maintain Encounter Care-Place Association` — Binds the encounter to physical wards, rooms, and beds over time.
- *Exposed Service*: `Encounter Location History Query` — Discloses patient location tracking history.
- *Function*: `Receive Order Request` — Ingests structured orders containing clinical indication, requesting clinician, and test specifications.
- *Exposed Service*: `Order Requisition Ingress` — Ingests electronic orders from clinical ordering systems.
- *Function*: `Resolve Order Destination` — Evaluates order routing rules to determine target laboratory, imaging centre, or procedural unit.
- *Exposed Service*: `Order Dispatch Service` — Transmits orders to performing diagnostic systems.

- *Function*: `Manage Order Progression` — Tracks order state (**scoped diagnostic/procedural illustration**): *Placed* $\to$ *Received* $\to$ *Specimen Collected* $\to$ *In-Progress* $\to$ *Preliminary Result* $\to$ *Final Result* $\to$ *Closed*.
- *Exposed Service*: `Order Status & Tracking Query` — Provides real-time order tracking to ordering clinicians.
- *Function*: `Coordinate Order Modification / Cancellation` — Handles requests to amend clinical details or cancel unexecuted orders.
- *Exposed Service*: `Order Cancellation Service` — Dispatches cancel directives to performing systems.
- *Function*: `Correlate Diagnostic Request` — Matches incoming lab/radiology results to active patient encounters and order requisitions.
- *Exposed Service*: `Diagnostic Correlation Resolution` — Discloses correlated order/result linkages.
- *Function*: `Bind Diagnostic Report` — Associates structured observations, reference ranges, and abnormal flags with patient health records.
- *Exposed Service*: `Diagnostic Report Ingress` — Ingests results from external LIS/RIS systems.
- *Function*: `Distribute Diagnostic Report` — Delivers preliminary, final, and corrected reports to ordering and copied practitioners.
- *Exposed Service*: `Diagnostic Result Delivery Service` — Emits secure result notifications.
- *Function*: `Receive Medication Order` — Ingests inpatient and outpatient drug prescriptions.
- *Exposed Service*: `Medication Order Ingress` — Ingests prescription events.
- *Function*: `Track Dispense Event` — Ingests community and hospital pharmacy dispensing records.
- *Exposed Service*: `Dispense Event Ingress` — Ingests pharmacy supply notifications.

- *Function*: `Receive Medication Administration Event` — Records medication administration-event information, including nurse-administered doses, e-MAR documentation and infusion telemetry as non-exhaustive examples; scope is not limited to nursing, bedside or inpatient settings.
- *Exposed Service*: `Medication Administration Ingress` — Ingests administration records.
- *Function*: `Receive Procedure Booking / Request` — Ingests procedural and surgical requisitions.
- *Exposed Service*: `Procedure Booking Ingress` — Receives surgical/procedural requests.
- *Function*: `Receive Procedural Documentation` — Ingests operation reports, anaesthetic records, and post-procedure notes.
- *Exposed Service*: `Procedural Documentation Ingress` — Ingests procedural documentation, including surgical notes, into patient record streams.
- *Function*: `Receive Clinical Document` — Receives clinical documents from information suppliers.
- *Exposed Service*: `Clinical Document Ingress` — Exposes document submission endpoints across the HIE.

- *Function*: `Govern Clinical Document Lifecycle` — Manages document states (**scoped illustration, not a universal transition model**): *Draft* $\to$ *Preliminary* $\to$ *Final* $\to$ *Amended* $\to$ *Superseded* $\to$ *Entered-in-Error*.
- *Exposed Service*: `Clinical Document Lifecycle Service` — Allows authoring clinicians to publish addenda or corrections.
- *Function*: `Index Clinical Document Metadata` — Indexes author, specialty, encounter, date, and document type (LOINC/SNOMED).
- *Exposed Service*: `Document Metadata Registry Query` — Discloses document registry metadata to clinical viewers.
- *Function*: `Receive Care Plan` — Ingests multidisciplinary care plans, clinical goals, and patient action steps.
- *Exposed Service*: `Care Plan Ingress` — Ingests shared care plans.
- *Function*: `Distribute Clinical Communication` — Routes secure messages, referral letters, and critical alerts to practitioner endpoints.
- *Exposed Service*: `Secure Clinical Message Dispatch` — Exposes message dispatch to clinical authors.
- *Function*: `Track Business Delivery Acknowledgement` — Tracks end-to-end delivery state and records business-level delivery/rejection acknowledgements.
- *Exposed Service*: `Communication Delivery Status Query` — Discloses delivery confirmation to message senders.
- *Function*: `Record Communication Transaction` — Maintains an immutable audit trail of clinical message dispatch and receipt.
- *Exposed Service*: `Communication Audit Query` — Discloses transmission history for medico-legal verification.
- *Function*: `Correlate Primary Care Consultation Context` — Binds GP consultation notes, vital signs, and encounter episodes to the regional Longitudinal Health Record (LHR).
- *Exposed Service*: `Primary Care Summary Ingress` — Ingests GP event summaries into the HIE.
- *Function*: `Assemble Acute Clinical Baseline` — Rapidly aggregates previous discharge summaries, active medications, allergies, and diagnostic alerts upon acute hospital presentation.
- *Exposed Service*: `Acute Admission Dossier Query` — Delivers a high-priority clinical briefing to admitting teams.
- *Function*: `Bind ED Triage Assessment` — Captures ATS (Australasian Triage Scale) category, presenting complaint, and ambulance paramedic handover data.
- *Exposed Service*: `ED Triage Stream Ingress` — Ingests emergency triage presentations.
- *Function*: `Provide Emergency LHR Summary` — Delivers rapid, override-capable access to Advance Care Directives, allergy records, and recent hospital admissions.
- *Exposed Service*: `Emergency Fast-Path LHR Query` — Provides low-latency emergency record summaries.
- *Function*: `Consolidate Inpatient Clinical Round Feed` — Aggregates daily vital signs, overnight pathology, allied health notes, and medication administration records.
- *Exposed Service*: `Ward Round Clinical Briefing Query` — Discloses consolidated 24-hour clinical briefing views.

- *Function*: `Project Longitudinal Medication History` — Aggregates community dispensing, hospital e-MAR administrations, and specialist prescriptions into a unified chronological medication profile.
- *Exposed Service*: `Longitudinal Medication History Query` — Discloses full medication timelines for medication reconciliation.
- *Function*: `Syndicate Immunisation Record` — Records vaccine encounters and syndicates records to national immunisation registers (e.g., AIR).
- *Exposed Service*: `Immunisation History Query` — Discloses complete vaccination history.
- *Function*: `Synchronize Community Visit Record` — Ingests clinical notes, wound assessments, and vital signs recorded in community and home settings.
- *Exposed Service*: `Community Care Encounter Ingress` — Ingests community care documentation.
- *Function*: `Provide Outreach Visit Context` — Packages and delivers portable clinical summaries and offline-capable care summaries for remote outreach clinics.
- *Function*: `Reconcile Outreach Clinical Batch` — Reconciles and merges clinical documentation recorded during disconnected remote clinic operations.
- *Exposed Service*: `Outreach Batch Reconciliation Service` — Reconciles batch clinical encounters upon network reconnection.
- *Function*: `Correlate Virtual Care Consultation Context` — Binds video consultation metadata, remote practitioner identity, and shared digital whiteboard artifacts to the encounter.
- *Exposed Service*: `Virtual Encounter Context Resolution` — Binds virtual session identifiers to patient encounters.
- *Function*: `Ingest Remote Patient Telemetry` — Ingests continuous or periodic physiological measurements (e.g., blood pressure, pulse oximetry, continuous glucose) from home monitoring devices.
- *Exposed Service*: `Remote Telemetry Ingress` — Ingests remote patient data streams into the LHR.
- *Function*: `Track Clinic Operating Session` — Ingests and tracks clinic operating-session start, delay and completion, distinct from an individual patient's queue progression.
- *Function*: `Manage Clinic Queue Progression` — Tracks patient arrival, rooming, consultation in-progress, and check-out states.
- *Exposed Service*: `Clinic Queue Telemetry Service` — Discloses real-time clinic waiting times and queue states.
- *Function*: `Assemble Ward Handover Context` — Collates current ward patient lists, active medical concerns and pending tasks for nursing shift handover.

- *Function*: `Manage Theatre Case Progression` — Coordinates surgical case milestones: *Case Called* $\to$ *Patient in Anaesthetic Bay* $\to$ *Anaesthesia Commenced* $\to$ *Knife to Skin* $\to$ *Procedure Finished* $\to$ *In PACU/Recovery* $\to$ *Ward Handover Complete*.
- *Exposed Service*: `Theatre Case Progression Telemetry` — Emits real-time surgical milestone updates.
- *Function*: `Capture Post-Clinic Follow-up Requirements` — Captures follow-up booking and diagnostic-order requirements generated at clinic completion.
- *Function*: `Maintain Operational Bed State` — Tracks real-time bed status and environmental locks.
- *Exposed Service*: `Bed Availability Query` — Discloses real-time bed availability across hospital directorates.

- *Function*: `Manage Bed Turnover Progression` — Coordinates cleaning, disinfection, and preparation: *Vacated* $\to$ *Cleaning Requested* $\to$ *Cleaning In-Progress* $\to$ *Inspected/Ready* $\to$ *Occupied*.
- *Exposed Service*: `Bed Turnover Lifecycle Service` — Coordinates turnover requests with environmental services.
- *Function*: `Track Mobile Clinical Asset Operational State` — Manages the real-time location and operational readiness of mobile ventilators, infusion pumps, and telemetry transmitters.
- *Exposed Service*: `Clinical Resource Availability Query` — Exposes mobile equipment availability.

- *Function*: `Aggregate Service Capacity Telemetry` — Consumes and coordinates context-specific service-capacity information for broader situational awareness, alongside bed occupancy, ICU surge capacity and ventilator availability across regional hospitals.
- *Exposed Service*: `Regional Health System Capacity Query` — Provides executive operational situational awareness.
- *Function*: `Receive Mobile Visit Progression` — Ingests arrival, visit-progression and safety check-in milestones from roving staff.

- *Function*: `Integrate Mobile Work Management` — Exchanges externally established work/assignment, dispatch and operational progression/status information, with applicable worker/context information, between mobile work-management mechanisms and Harmonia operational coordination.
- *Function*: `Resolve Active On-Call Coverage` — Resolves primary, secondary, and tertiary on-call clinical specialists for emergency escalation.
- *Exposed Service*: `On-Call Specialist Lookup` — Discloses active on-call contacts for switchboard and emergency teams.

- *Function*: `Dispatch Operational Work Order` — Allocates work requests to available wardspersons or support teams using applicable allocation policies, staff roles, credentials, location and skill, and delivers allocated work to the target worker, device or team queue.
- *Exposed Service*: `Work Dispatch Service` — Delivers allocated work and captures distinct technical and operational acknowledgements; acknowledgement alone does not establish completion.
- *Function*: `Manage Operational Work Progression` — Tracks execution states: *Queued* $\to$ *Assigned* $\to$ *Accepted* $\to$ *In-Progress* $\to$ *Completed / Aborted*.
- *Exposed Service*: `Operational Work Status Query` — Discloses task progression to requesting wards.

- *Function*: `Manage Patient Transport Progression` — Coordinates intra-facility and inter-facility patient movements: *Transport Requested* $\to$ *Porter Dispatched* $\to$ *Patient Collected* $\to$ *In-Transit* $\to$ *Delivered at Destination* $\to$ *Handover Completed*.
- *Exposed Service*: `Patient Transport Tracking Service` — Provides real-time transit telemetry.

- *Function*: `Manage Specimen Transport Progression` — Tracks the physical transit of pathology bio-specimens, blood products, and surgical trays: *Collected* $\to$ *Courier Picked Up* $\to$ *In-Transit* $\to$ *Laboratory Ingress Received*.
- *Exposed Service*: `Specimen Transit Tracking Service` — Exposes chain-of-custody tracking.

- *Function*: `Manage Discharge Coordination Progression` — Synchronises multi-agency discharge readiness (**illustrative preparation; publication, authorisation and confirmed exit are distinct**): *Discharge Planning Initiated* $\to$ *Medications Reconciled* $\to$ *Transport Booked* $\to$ *Discharge Summary Finalised* $\to$ *Physically Departed*.
- *Exposed Service*: `Discharge Readiness Telemetry` — Discloses discharge barrier checklists and planned departure times.

- *Function*: `Verify Clinical Qualification for Work Dispatch` — Validates that a practitioner possesses active clinical credentials and required competency certificates before dispatch of specialised work.

- *Function*: `Assemble Longitudinal Clinical Record` — Synthesises clinical documents, encounters, diagnostic reports, and medication histories across disparate source systems into a unified chronological clinical view.
- *Exposed Service*: `Longitudinal Clinical Record Query` — Discloses the comprehensive clinical timeline to authorised clinicians.
- *Function*: `Maintain Active Clinical Record` — Maintains active problem lists, current medication regimens, allergies, and open clinical alerts for active care coordination.
- *Exposed Service*: `Active Problem & Allergy Summary Query` — Exposes immediate active clinical summaries.

- *Function*: `Preserve Durable Clinical Record` — Preserves the governed longitudinal representation and durable, immutable, append-only history of what Harmonia received, knew, asserted or managed, with provenance and versioning. Corrections/supersession establish changed knowledge without retrospectively altering that history or acquiring originating clinical authority.

- *Exposed Service*: `Historical Clinical Record Access` — Provides governed historical record retrieval for authorised clinical and legal review; preservation does not itself establish legal qualification or originating authority.
- *Function*: `Receive Information Submission` — Validates and ingests standards-compliant clinical messages from external health providers.
- *Exposed Service*: `HIE Submission Gateway Service` — Ingress endpoint for regional data contributions.
- *Function*: `Mediate Information Retrieval` — Federates queries across participating hospital and diagnostic node repositories.
- *Exposed Service*: `Federated Health Information Query` — Resolves distributed record queries.
- *Function*: `Distribute Addressed Information` — Directs point-to-point clinical documents to specific recipient practitioner endpoints.
- *Exposed Service*: `Addressed Document Delivery Service` — Securely delivers documents to designated recipient mailboxes.
- *Function*: `Syndicate Information Change` — Broadcasts event notifications and record updates to subscribed regional care network systems.
- *Exposed Service*: `Clinical Event Syndication Stream` — Emits publish-subscribe clinical event feeds.
- *Function*: `Search Health Information` — Executes structured semantic searches across diagnostic reports, clinical notes, and medication histories.
- *Exposed Service*: `Clinical Information Search Service` — Discloses search capabilities to clinical user interfaces.
- *Function*: `Mediate Standards-Based Health Information Communication` — Handles standards-based communication mediation, transaction coordination, and technical error handling.
- *Exposed Service*: `Standards Communication Gateway Service` — Protocol interface for external client integrations.
- *Function*: `Evaluate Information Access Authority` — Evaluates user role, organisation, patient relationship, purpose of use, and break-glass overrides against default-deny policies.
- *Exposed Service*: `Policy Evaluation & Authorisation Service` — Evaluates access requests across the platform.
- *Function*: `Record Security-Significant Activity` — Records tamper-evident audit evidence (who, what, when, why, patient MRN, policy outcome) without logging unmasked PHI.
- *Exposed Service*: `Security Audit Ingress` — Ingests audit events across all capabilities.
- *Function*: `Resolve Clinical Concept` — Validates concept identifiers and retrieves preferred clinical rubrics and hierarchy paths.
- *Exposed Service*: `Terminology Concept Resolution Service` — Exposes concept validation lookups.
- *Function*: `Map Clinical Concept` — Translates local lab codes and legacy terms to canonical SNOMED/LOINC codes using governed translation maps.
- *Exposed Service*: `Terminology Mapping Service` — Translates codes across terminology systems.
- *Function*: `Coordinate Care-Team Collaboration` — Manages care-team communication spaces, participant memberships, and clinical handovers.
- *Exposed Service*: `Clinical Collaboration Space Service` — Manages team collaboration spaces and discussions.
- *Function*: `Resolve LHR Query within Collaboration` — Contextually projects active patient summaries directly into collaborative clinical discussion channels.
- *Exposed Service*: `Collaboration Clinical Summary Resolution` — Embeds clinical summaries in collaboration feeds.
- *Function*: `Govern Collaboration Metadata` — Enforces privacy policies, participant access gates, and zero-PHI space metadata rules.
- *Exposed Service*: `Collaboration Space Governance Service` — Governs space lifecycles and membership.
- *Function*: `Coordinate Operational Collaboration` — Provides communication spaces for facility logistics, disaster management teams, and administrative committees.
- *Exposed Service*: `Operational Collaboration Service` — Provides non-clinical operational messaging channels.
- *Function*: `Coordinate Work Order` — Coordinates operational task lifecycles and dispatches.
- *Exposed Service*: `Work Order Coordination Service` — Manages operational work progression.

- *Function*: `Coordinate To Do` — Coordinates human review/update/approval items, reminders and sign-off queues within Harmonia's operational responsibility; clinical requirements and decisions remain with accountable clinical authority.
- *Exposed Service*: `To Do Management Service` — Provides To Do inbox and sign-off coordination without acquiring underlying clinical-work management.
- *Function*: `Coordinate Synthetic Task` — Orchestrates automated system workflows and operational progression.
- *Exposed Service*: `Synthetic Task Execution Service` — Coordinates automated tasks.
- *Function*: `Supervise Activity Timeout / Escalation` — Monitors SLAs and triggers escalations when clinical or operational deadlines elapse.
- *Exposed Service*: `Activity Escalation Telemetry` — Discloses SLA breaches.
- *Function*: `Project Operational Schedule` — Aggregates and overlays multidisciplinary schedules onto a unified temporal view.
- *Exposed Service*: `Unified Calendar Projection Query` — Discloses consolidated temporal schedules.
- *Function*: `Correlate Activity with Temporal Context` — Associates clinical events with shift boundaries and appointment slots.
- *Exposed Service*: `Temporal Context Resolution` — Resolves operational shifts.
- *Function*: `Present Contextual Health and Operational Information` — Composes clinical summaries, work queues, and patient records into responsive role-based user interfaces.
- *Exposed Service*: `Contextual Presentation Service` — Delivers contextual health and operational information for presentation.
- *Function*: `Govern Information Semantics` — Authors and validates canonical data concepts and entity relationships.
- *Exposed Service*: `Semantic Model Definition Service` — Discloses canonical model definitions.
- *Function*: `Verify Semantic Conformance` — Validates candidate messages against canonical governance schemas.
- *Exposed Service*: `Semantic Conformance Verification Service` — Validates representations for compliance.

Service provision joins a named offering to the organisations, places and practitioner roles through which it is provided. The mapping is the owned concern; the identity and meaning of each mapped participant remain with its established capability.

Regular hours, on-call windows and exceptional closures describe when an offering is nominally available. They provide an input to readiness and scheduling without proving that all required dependencies are ready.

Published catchment, referral and clinical eligibility conditions explain the intended audience and access constraints of an offering. Their representation supports responsible assessment without deciding acceptance or clinical priority.

An identifiable physical device carries UDI and serial context through its use. The instance record supports association and resolution without originating device observations or making maintenance decisions.

A device can be associated with different patients and care places at different times. Qualified association and its lineage allow observations to be interpreted against the applicable binding rather than the current assignment alone.

A device communication binding identifies the protocol and endpoint through which its feed can participate. Connectivity metadata supports routing without owning authentication issuance, payload semantics or physiological interpretation.

Coordinate the intake, care-request disposition and appointment information through which a person accesses care. Its constituent abilities distinguish Client-Centred Administration; Referral Administration; Scheduling Administration.

Maintain distinguishable care-episode, bounded fulfilment and delivered-activity information across performing systems. Its constituent abilities distinguish Episode & Encounter Administration; Order Administration; Diagnostic Administration; Medication Administration; Procedure Administration.

Administer the lifecycle, shared-plan context and directed communication of care documentation. Its constituent abilities distinguish Clinical Record Administration; Care Plan Administration; Clinical Communication Administration.

Represent coverage context and convey care-activity evidence to responsible funding and charging systems. Its constituent abilities distinguish Funding & Coverage Administration; Clinical Charging & Claims Administration.

Support continuity, remote participation and preventive follow-up through appropriately assembled and exchanged care context. Its constituent abilities distinguish Primary Care; Community Care; Outreach Care; Remote & Virtual Care; Preventive Care.

Provide the context assemblies and boundary integration needed for facility presentations and bounded care episodes. Its constituent abilities distinguish Acute Care; Emergency Care; Inpatient Care; Ambulatory Care; Surgical & Procedural Care.

Integrate specialist assessment, investigation and therapeutic information with longitudinal and episode context. Its constituent abilities distinguish Clinical Assessment; Diagnostic Services; Therapeutic Services; Medication Therapy; Allied Health; Rehabilitation.

Coordinate the local flow, session state and capacity semantics of a care-delivery setting. Its constituent abilities distinguish Clinic & Practice Operations; Ward Operations; Theatre Operations; Emergency Department Operations; Outpatient Operations.

Relate operational care-place and equipment state to the coordinated view of service demand and capacity. Its constituent abilities distinguish Bed & Care-Place Management; Clinical Resource Management; Service Capacity Management.

Make workforce availability, coverage and eligible operational work participation usable in coordination. Its constituent abilities distinguish Clinical Workforce Management; Clinical Rostering; Mobile Staff Management; On-Call Management; Work Allocation & Dispatch.

Represent learning, competence, professional-standing checks and separately governed operational access qualifications. Its constituent abilities distinguish Clinical Training & Education; Clinical Competency Management; Clinical Qualification Management; Clinical Supervision; Credential Management.

Coordinate movement of people/materials and operational departure readiness across care boundaries. Its constituent abilities distinguish Patient Transport; Clinical Logistics Coordination; Discharge Management.
Maintain governed longitudinal synthesis and the associations needed to use its constituent clinical information safely. Its constituent abilities distinguish Patient Clinical Record.

Make governed health information discoverable and exchangeable under explicit internal and external contracts. Its constituent abilities distinguish Health Information Exchange; Health Information Access; Health Information Communication.

Govern the definitions, terminology and reference content that make healthcare information consistently interpretable. Its constituent abilities distinguish Clinical Knowledge Services; Information Design Governance.
Apply information-use policy and preserve the accountability context needed for governed health-information activity. Its constituent abilities distinguish Health Information Control.

Support contextual discussion and human interaction with governed information and activity. Its constituent abilities distinguish Clinical Collaboration; General Collaboration; Presentation Services.

Consumers need an identifiable statement of which rule applies and who established it. This proposal fills BC-17 information support without giving the platform authority to make legislation, approve governance requirements or reinterpret their force.

Activity concerning the same patient, practitioner or bed needs a coherent entity-relative frame. Interest fan-out, serial progression, fresh information context and uncertain effects remain distinguishable from generic multi-work-unit progression.

An activity needs a fulfilment definition even when only one bounded execution unit is involved. This capability specifies its semantic envelope while execution and event delivery remain separate responsibilities.

Collective readiness depends on suitable workforce, spaces, equipment, materials and supporting services. This proposal evaluates their joint availability for an offering without treating one available bed, an operating-hours declaration or aggregate capacity as service readiness.

Interpret observed clinical findings and their significance for the individual care concern. The proposed decomposition separates this outcome from the other responsibilities within Clinical Determination.
Establish and qualify the clinical problems or diagnoses applicable to an individual. The proposed decomposition separates this outcome from the other responsibilities within Clinical Determination.
Establish clinically meaningful risk and expected-course judgements for an individual. The proposed decomposition separates this outcome from the other responsibilities within Clinical Determination.

Establish the intended outcomes and priorities against which an individual care response is planned. The proposed decomposition separates this outcome from the other responsibilities within Individual Care Planning.

Determine the intended clinical response and its sequencing in relation to agreed care goals. The proposed decomposition separates this outcome from the other responsibilities within Individual Care Planning.

Prepare or compound a clinically required medication formulation under the applicable professional and product-governance mandate. The proposed decomposition separates this outcome from the other responsibilities within Medication & Pharmacy Services.

Preparedness asks whether the service as a whole can operate, distinct from scheduling capacity or readiness of a single place. This is a proposed missing business frame for the already identified readiness concern.
Entity integrity, context, lifecycle, information maintenance, discovery and semantic conformance are constituent reusable abilities; none is an implementation subsystem.
Requests, events, work and human interaction are related ways to cause or observe change, with distinct contracts and progression responsibilities.

Policy, evidence, resilience and independent assurance contribute to confidence through different responsibilities. Keeping them as peers prevents technical success or recorded evidence from becoming a business assurance conclusion.
Active representation, observation and convergence support availability while preserving an explicit trust basis for use.
Durable acceptance gives managed information an explicit committed state from which applicable active representations can be reconstructed.
Document attachments, diagnostic media and operational artefacts share a need to locate usable content while distinguishing logical meaning from physical possession.
Permission depends on controlled criteria, role assignments, action and information scope; revocation is distinct from natural expiry.
Distributed participants apply the applicable effective authorisation and fail closed when authority is absent or untrustworthy.
Lineage explains how an assertion reached its present form without turning every infrastructure event into provenance.
Denied actions and successful mutations may both require trustworthy evidence; the audited identity and capture authority remain distinct.
The semantic execution envelope applies to one-step and multi-step activity and stays distinct from dispatch and supervision.
Reusable execution control respects work-unit archetype, participation and uncertain effects rather than equating dispatch with completion.
Patient, practitioner and bed concerns recur across different business contexts; each can need a coherent progression frame without one central entity service.

Identity correlation, clinical-history synthesis, reference-content use and assurance evidence all need to distinguish the standing of an assertion from technical acceptance. This recurring ability is insufficiently explicit in the existing fourteen EC definitions and is proposed as a new peer responsibility.

canonical_id_policy.authority: Explicit task authorisation for v0.1 identifier allocation; RAD metamodel §8 controls structural semantics.

canonical_id_policy.other: BEC tiers and complete ancestry unresolved under K9; Features and owned behaviour cannot receive speculative structural paths.
